title: Degree of Comparison
theory:
 Degree of comparison refers to the different forms of an adjective used to show the level of
      quality, quantity, or intensity when comparing one, two, or more persons/things.
      Degree of comparison dk vFkZ gS adjective ds fofHkUu :iksa dk ç;ksx djds xq.koÙkk] ek=kk ;k rhozrk dk
      Lrj fn•kuk] tc ,d nks ;k vf/d O;fDr;ksa ;k oLrqvksa dh rqyuk dh tkrh gSA
   Three degrees of comparison

       Positive degree                Shows no comparison.
       Comparative degree             To compare two persons or things.
       Superlative degree             To compare more than two persons or things.
      Examples
   		 1. Ram is tall.		 2. Ram is taller than Shyam.                       3. Ram is the tallest in the class.
     Comparison in Positive degree to show equality / inequality
 		 Part A – Subject1 + Verb + So/as + Positive degree adjective + as + Subject2
 		 Part B – No other + Subject1 + Verb + So/as + Positive degree adjective + as + Subject2
     Comparison in comparative degree
                                                                               +Any other + Singular Noun
    Subject + Verb + Comparative degree adjective + than
                                                                               +All other + Plural Noun
     Comparison in Superlative degree
       Subject + Verb + the + Superlative degree adjective + of + all + Plural Noun
     Points to Remember
     1 One of + Superlative degree
     2 By far + Superlative degree
     3 Do not use "other" after "all" in case of Superlative Degree. (All + Superlative)
     4 Double Comparatives and double Superlatives are not allowed.
